text:
anya: Heads-up — nightly eval alerted on pset v10 rebaseline. Large jump in negation failures and some hallucination regressions. Alert: https://ci.redwood/evals/alerts/pset-v10-1742109876 :eyes:
ci-bot: nightly-eval job #4421 finished. baseline=pset_v9 -> candidate=pset_v10. metric_deltas: negation_f1: -6.2%, halluc_rate: +1.8%, exact_match: -0.4%. threshold_exceeded: true
raj: Ugh. Do we have the pset diff? can someone paste the top-level changes?
maria: Pulled the diff now — most edits are prompt wording simplifications and ~120 label fixes. But there are 6 new negative-case paraphrases that might be too subtle. Snippet of diff:
```
- When would the user NOT want to do X?
+ Are there times the user should avoid X?
```
sam: That specific wording change is suspicious for negation handling. Candidate model is same as prod; only pset changed.
lia: Can we run a quick canary re-eval only for negation subset? I can spin up the query set now.
raj: Yes please. Lia, run against model=rwd-instruct-2025-3, pset=negation-subset v10-preview and paste results.
lia: Ran it — negation_f1 on subset dropped 9.1% (v9: 92.4 -> v10: 83.3). Raw examples look like missed "doesn't" cases.
anya: So cause is pset change not model. Two options: rollback pset -> v9 or rebaseline (accept new ground truth). We should prefer rollback if our changes accidentally changed labeling intent.
maria: I reviewed a random sample of 200 diffs. ~15% are ambiguous rephrasings that tilt the label. I lean rollback.
sam: Product input needed here — is the new phrasing intentional product-led clarification? If yes, rebaseline might be okay but we need to surface to customers.
anya: @raj can you ping @product for quick decision? I don't want us to ship this into canary.
raj: ping @product (cc: @design) — is the new pset wording aligned with product intent or should we revert? :wave:
raj: product responded in threads — they intended clarifications but not to change behavior. They want parity with old labeling.
anya: OK decision: rollback pset to v9 for the nightly pipeline. We'll create a hotfix PR to revert the pset commit and re-run nightly. Also add stricter diffs checks on negation tokens.
lia: For rollback: git command to revert the pset commit is:
```
# from evals repo
git checkout main
git revert --no-edit 0f3a9bc --no-verify
git push origin main
```
sam: Can someone approve the PR once created? I'll review tests.
maria: I'll write a short postmortem paragraph for the release notes explaining accidental label drift and the rollback.
anya: After rollback we should add an automated check: if negation_subset_delta > 2% then block rebaseline without human sign-off. Lia, can you file an issue?
lia: Filed: https://github.com/redwood/evals/issues/523 — "negation delta gate for pset updates". Added minimal repro and suggested threshold.
raj: Created PR #783 to revert pset v10. @sam @anya please approve if ok. Link: https://github.com/redwood/evals/pull/783
sam: Reviewing now. Quick sanity: add the failing examples as fixtures so we don't regress.
anya: Agreed — add 30 edge-case fixtures to negation-suite. I can draft them.
ci-bot: deploybot: nightly pipeline re-trigger requested by raj. job #4422 queued.
lia: Nightly re-run (post-rollback) shows metrics back to baseline: negation_f1 delta = +0.1%. Good.
maria: Thanks team. We should schedule a short policy doc for pset wording changes and rebaseline approvals. I'll draft and ping legal for implications later.
anya: Final status: rollback done, PR merged, gating issue created, fixtures added. Marking as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
